title: Demo · Cheating under the IPC, co-accused already on bail
story: Accused-1 is charged under IPC 420 and 406 for taking an advance of Rs. 6,50,000 for machinery that was never delivered; the offence (March 2024) predates the BNS, so the IPC governs. He has been in custody since 12.03.2024, the charge sheet was filed in time and the trial is under way; his earlier bail application was rejected, while Co-accused-2, with a comparable role, is on bail.

variant.offence: IPC 420/406 cheating (maximum 7 years), offence before 1 July 2024
variant.custody: default bail closed (charge sheet on day 55 of 60); past one-third of the maximum as a first-time offender (BNSS s.479 ELIGIBLE: 978 days against 852)
variant.parity: Co-accused-2 granted bail; first-time offender; earlier bail application rejected

steps.title: Rights Radar
steps.caption: At intake Peshkar ran the 7 rules of the Rights Radar on the dossier as of 2026-11-15: date arithmetic and statute tables, not the language model. Default bail: WINDOW_CLOSED, Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479): ELIGIBLE, Production within 24 hours: CHECK and Antil category: CHECK. Each result names its rule and the dates it used; rules not yet re-checked against the bare act are marked unverified.

filled.label: Default bail
filled.value: WINDOW_CLOSED: 60-day limit (maximum 7 years). Day 1 is the first remand, 13.03.2024. The charge sheet was filed on day 55 (06.05.2024). It came within the limit, so the right to default bail never arose.

filled.label: Undertrial limit (BNSS s.479)
filled.value: ELIGIBLE: 978 days in custody. The threshold is 852 days for a first-time offender (1/3 of 7 years, on bond) and 1,278 days otherwise (1/2, on bail). The applicable threshold (1/3, first-time offender) of 852 days has been reached. The record shows no other pending case (BNSS s.479(2)).

filled.label: Notice of appearance
filled.value: UNKNOWN: Offence punishable up to 7 years. No arrest memo or notice in the file.

filled.label: Grounds of arrest
filled.value: UNKNOWN: No record that the grounds of arrest were communicated.

filled.label: Production within 24 hours
filled.value: CHECK: Produced the next day; times not on record.

filled.label: Antil category
filled.value: CHECK: Category A (up to 7 years), unless treated as an economic offence (D). Antil's categories decide how an accused who was not arrested during investigation and cooperated is treated after the charge sheet; for a client in custody this is context, not a bail entitlement.

filled.label: Statutory bar
filled.value: NOT_APPLICABLE: No NDPS, UAPA or PMLA section is charged.

steps.title: Abhiyojak argues the other side
steps.caption: Abhiyojak, the prosecution sparring partner, raised 16 objections in 2 rounds, each grounded in a prosecution argument from comparable orders or a fact of the case; 4 ungrounded objections were discarded. Abhiyojak judged 0 of Vakeel's replies: 0 answered, 0 partly answered, 0 unanswered; 16 objections could not be judged because the sparring token budget was spent, and stay unanswered. Whatever stays open is listed at Gate 2, and counsel answers it before approving.

filled.label: O1 against G1 (gravity and punishment)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The gravity of the offence and the severity of the prescribed punishment are material factors that must be weighed against the presumption of bail, particularly where the maximum punishment exceeds five years and the offence is non-bailable.

filled.label: O2 against G2 (custody period)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The offences under IPC 420 (BNS 318(4)), carrying a maximum punishment of 7 years, and IPC 406 (BNS 316(2)), carrying a maximum punishment of 3 years, are serious economic offences that warrant continued custody pending trial.

filled.label: O3 against G3 (charge sheet filed)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The offences are non-bailable, carrying a maximum punishment of 7 years and 3 years respectively, and involve cheating and criminal breach of trust, indicating the gravity of the allegations is substantial.

filled.label: O4 against G3 (charge sheet filed)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant has been in custody for 978 days, yet the investigation is complete and the charge sheet filed, raising serious concerns about whether the applicant would abscond if released, given the prolonged delay in proceedings.

filled.value: UNANSWERED: The defence relies on the pendency of criminal cases not being a basis for refusal of bail, but the State has not shown exceptional circumstances to deny bail on the ground of criminal antecedents, and the charge-sheet has been filed in the present case.

filled.label: O10 against G7 (weak prima facie)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The ground relies on a prima facie case and the nature of supporting evidence, yet the record does not demonstrate that the prosecution has taken any steps to ensure the safety of witnesses or to mitigate the risk of tampering if the applicant is released.

filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant has not undergone half of the maximum sentence for the offence under IPC 420 (BNS 318(4)), which carries a maximum punishment of 7 years, as required under Section 436A of the CrPC.

filled.label: O12 against G9 (undertrial period)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant has not undergone half of the minimum sentence prescribed for the offence under IPC 420 (BNS 318(4)), which carries a minimum sentence of 7 years, as required under the first proviso to Section 436A of the CrPC.

filled.label: O13 against general (gravity and punishment)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The offences charged under IPC 420 and IPC 406 are non-bailable with maximum punishments of 7 years and 3 years respectively, indicating the gravity of the offences is substantial and warrants continued custody pending trial.

filled.label: O14 against general (flight risk)
filled.value: UNANSWERED: The applicant has no passport, yet the prosecution must still consider the possibility of flight risk given the economic nature of the offence and the potential for the applicant to abscond if released.
